opportunities.name: Certified payroll / prevailing wage weekly reporting
opportunities.buyer: Subcontractors on public-works projects, 5-40 field employees

pain.note: Weekly WH-347 filing is legally mandatory on federally funded jobs; errors withhold payment

recurrence.note: Weekly, for the life of every public project

willingness_to_pay.note: Fully managed certified payroll services run $1,000-$5,000/mo for mid-sized contractors; software tier is $50-175/mo

deal_size.note: Managed pricing of $1,000+/mo means $10K needs only 10 customers

reachability.note: Public bid awards and state contractor license boards list them for free

automation.note: Form assembly + wage-determination cross-check from a payroll export; deterministic, checkable

speed_to_revenue.note: Deliverable from a spreadsheet they email - no integration needed

whitespace.note: Managed providers already exist - Points North, eBacon managed tier, CPWIS, regional construction bookkeepers

low_regulatory_risk.note: No license needed to prepare, but a filing error withholds the customer's payment and can trigger DOL penalties; we would also hold employee SSNs and wage data

opportunities.notes: Upgraded after research: the managed-service tier is a proven $1,000-5,000/mo purchase, which fixes the deal-size weakness. Remaining risks are liability on errors, weekly rather than monthly cadence, and a steep prevailing-wage learning curve. Designated fallback if OPP-08 fails.

opportunities.name: Lien waiver + AIA pay application preparation
opportunities.buyer: Specialty subcontractors billing on commercial projects

pain.note: Monthly billing packages are notoriously fiddly and delay payment when wrong

willingness_to_pay.note: Construction billing software exists; direct service pricing not verified

reachability.note: State license boards publish searchable contractor registries

automation.note: Document assembly is automatable; chasing lower-tier waivers is human coordination

speed_to_revenue.note: Requires learning each GC's billing conventions

whitespace.note: Incumbents are ERP modules priced for larger contractors

low_regulatory_risk.note: Lien waivers are legal instruments; preparation is clerical but consequential

opportunities.notes: Assumption-heavy. Needs pricing evidence before it can outrank the researched options.

opportunities.name: Permit application prep & tracking
opportunities.buyer: HVAC, electrical, plumbing contractors doing 20+ permits/month

pain.note: Every jurisdiction differs; rejections delay revenue

willingness_to_pay.note: Permit expediters exist as a local service category; pricing not verified

automation.note: Many jurisdictions require portal submission under the contractor's own account

speed_to_revenue.note: Jurisdiction knowledge takes time to build

low_regulatory_risk.note: Some jurisdictions restrict who may pull permits

opportunities.notes: Portal-submission requirement is the likely blocker - needs the contractor's credentials.

opportunities.name: COI / subcontractor insurance compliance tracking
opportunities.buyer: General contractors and property owners managing 50-500 vendors

pain.note: An expired COI on a claim is an uninsured loss

reachability.note: GCs are listed publicly, but the buyer is a risk manager behind a gatekeeper

automation.note: Extraction from certificates and expiry chasing is highly automatable

whitespace.note: At least seven established platforms compete directly

low_regulatory_risk.note: Insurance adjacent; we track, we do not advise

opportunities.notes: Demand proven by pricing, but the category is mature and crowded. Whitespace is the weak factor.

opportunities.name: Government bid monitoring + proposal drafting
opportunities.buyer: SMB contractors and service firms pursuing public contracts

pain.note: An established consulting category exists precisely because this is painful

recurrence.note: Continuous monitoring plus per-bid response work

willingness_to_pay.note: Multiple firms sell proposal writing to small business; retainer pricing not published

reachability.note: SAM.gov registrants and past bidders are public and free

automation.note: Monitoring automates cleanly; proposal drafting needs heavy human review

whitespace.note: Incumbents price for larger firms; SMB tier underserved

opportunities.notes: Best deal size in the set. Weakness: value is speculative to the buyer - they pay now to maybe win later - and QA on long proposals is expensive in founder hours.

opportunities.name: OSHA safety documentation & toolbox talk program

pain.note: Painful only after an incident or an audit

opportunities.notes: Low willingness to pay - the problem is only urgent after it is too late.

opportunities.name: Missed-call / speed-to-lead answering for home services

pain.note: A missed call is a lost job - the pain is obvious and quantifiable

willingness_to_pay.note: Answering services are an established purchase

zero_cost_feasibility.note: Telephony infrastructure and 24/7 coverage both cost money from day one

low_regulatory_risk.note: Call recording consent laws vary by state

kill_flags: Requires paid telephony infrastructure before the first dollar - violates the $0 constraint
Requires 24/7 real-time coverage - cannot be QA'd inside 6-10 founder hours/week
opportunities.notes: Real pain, wrong constraints. Killed on the $0 and capacity disqualifiers, not on demand.

opportunities.name: HOA board meeting minutes + post-meeting action package

pain.note: Minutes are a statutory record; managers write them after hours, unpaid, days later

recurrence.note: Every association holds board meetings on a fixed monthly or quarterly cycle

willingness_to_pay.note: MinuteSmith $149-699/mo by portfolio size, Enterprise from $12,000/yr; BoardBreeze $29.99-499/mo

deal_size.note: Portfolio managers carry 8-12 associations each, so a mid-size firm runs 25-50 board meetings/month; at $75/meeting that is $1,875-3,750/mo - $10K needs only 4-6 customers

reachability.note: 8,000-9,000 management companies manage 60-70% of ~377,000 US associations; managers are state-licensed and publicly searchable in FL, NV, and others

automation.note: Audio to structured minutes is language work end to end; motions/votes/actions are template-shaped

speed_to_revenue.note: Deliverable on day one from a recording they already have - no integration, no credentials

zero_cost_feasibility.note: This repo already contains a working audio-extraction pipeline; delivery is a document

whitespace.note: Incumbents sell self-serve software to the manager who still does the work; done-for-you at portfolio level is a different wedge

low_regulatory_risk.note: No license to draft minutes, but CA/FL/PA are two-party consent states - the board must announce recording. Industry-standard mitigation is announce, transcribe, then delete the audio

opportunities.notes: Best deal-size-to-effort ratio in the set, and the only opportunity where we can deliver a complete free sample within 24 hours at zero cost. Chief unknown, and the first thing outreach must test: what share of associations already record their meetings.

opportunities.name: Municipal / public board meeting minutes
opportunities.buyer: Cities, towns, school districts, water and fire districts

pain.note: Open-meeting laws mandate minutes; clerks are stretched

willingness_to_pay.note: Public bodies budget for clerk services and transcription

reachability.note: Every public body publishes its contacts by law

automation.note: Meetings are already recorded and often streamed publicly

speed_to_revenue.note: Public procurement, budget cycles, and possible RFP requirements

low_regulatory_risk.note: Public records law raises the accuracy bar

opportunities.notes: Same delivery engine as OPP-08 with a far slower sales cycle. A phase-two market, not a launch market.

opportunities.name: Real estate transaction coordination

recurrence.note: Per transaction, and agent volume is lumpy

deal_size.note: An agent doing 3 files/mo is ~$1,200; but most agents do far fewer

reachability.note: Licensed agents are publicly listed everywhere

automation.note: The job is chasing humans for signatures and deadlines - phone work, not document work

whitespace.note: Thousands of independent TCs plus several funded AI entrants

low_regulatory_risk.note: Unlicensed assistants are restricted from some activities in some states

opportunities.notes: Proven demand, but the work is real-time human coordination - the opposite of what AI leverage is good at.

opportunities.name: Property maintenance ticket triage & vendor dispatch
kill_flags: Requires real-time response during business hours - cannot be delivered inside 6-10 founder hours/week
Requires write access to the customer's property management system
opportunities.notes: Genuinely painful, structurally incompatible with a part-time founder.

opportunities.name: HOA violation & architectural review letter production

pain.note: High volume, templated, and legally sensitive

willingness_to_pay.note: Often bundled into existing management software

reachability.note: Same buyer as OPP-08, publicly licensed

low_regulatory_risk.note: Enforcement letters have due-process requirements that vary by state

opportunities.notes: Best value as an expansion offer to OPP-08 customers, not as a standalone wedge.

opportunities.name: Lease abstraction for small commercial owners

recurrence.note: Mostly one-off at acquisition or refinance

opportunities.notes: Fails the recurrence test. Lumpy project revenue cannot be reverse-engineered to a reliable $10K/mo.

opportunities.name: Monthly board financial packet assembly

pain.note: Monthly packets are a known crunch for portfolio managers

automation.note: Requires accounting data from their system

opportunities.notes: Another natural expansion offer for the OPP-08 buyer. Needs their accounting exports.

opportunities.name: Dental insurance verification (eligibility & breakdowns)

pain.note: In-house verification staff costs roughly $3,600/mo fully loaded

reachability.note: State dental boards publish licensee rosters

automation.note: Requires logging into payer portals and the practice management system

whitespace.note: Established outsourcing firms compete directly on price

low_regulatory_risk.note: PHI throughout; requires a HIPAA business associate agreement

kill_flags: Requires the customer's payer-portal and practice-management credentials - a system we cannot access on our own terms
PHI handling requires a HIPAA business associate agreement before the first delivery
opportunities.notes: The clearest ROI story in the entire set, and still correctly killed: the constraints, not the demand, make it wrong for us right now.

opportunities.name: Dental/medical claim denial follow-up (AR recovery)
opportunities.buyer: Practices with aging AR over 90 days

pain.note: Unrecovered AR is money already earned and not collected

willingness_to_pay.note: Contingency pricing removes the buying objection entirely

automation.note: Payer phone queues and portal work

speed_to_revenue.note: Contingency means getting paid only after recovery lands

kill_flags: PHI and practice-management system access required
Delivery is phone work with payers - not compatible with 6-10 founder hours/week
opportunities.notes: Excellent economics, incompatible constraints.

opportunities.name: Patient recall & reactivation campaigns
opportunities.buyer: Dental practices with lapsed hygiene patients

pain.note: Lost revenue, but invisible day to day

whitespace.note: Every practice management vendor ships this

low_regulatory_risk.note: Patient lists are PHI; TCPA applies to texting

opportunities.notes: Bundled free into software the practice already owns. Weak wedge.

opportunities.name: Provider credentialing & re-credentialing paperwork
opportunities.buyer: Small practices and staffing firms onboarding clinicians
opportunities.notes: No PHI, which saves it from the healthcare kill list - but the domain learning curve is steep and revenue is per-hire, not recurring.

opportunities.name: Prior authorization packet assembly
kill_flags: Clinical documentation and PHI at the core of every deliverable
Requires clinical judgment the founder cannot quality-check
opportunities.notes: Highest pain in the healthcare set and the least appropriate for us to touch.

opportunities.name: Medical record chronology for personal injury firms

pain.note: A 1,200-page file takes ~40 paralegal hours at ~$85/hr loaded, about $3,400 in-house

recurrence.note: Per case; firms run continuous caseloads

willingness_to_pay.note: Outsourced review of that file runs about $4,500; AI chronologies $28-125

reachability.note: Bar directories and firm websites are public

whitespace.note: At least eight AI chronology products compete, with prices already down to $28

low_regulatory_risk.note: PHI under a HIPAA business associate agreement, plus legal work product

opportunities.notes: Textbook pain, and the price is already collapsing under funded AI entrants. Arriving late to a commoditizing market with $0 is the wrong fight.

opportunities.name: Inbound sales order / PO entry for SMB distributors
opportunities.buyer: Wholesale distributors receiving orders by email and PDF

pain.note: Manual entry runs 6-15 minutes per order; at 100 orders/day that is multiple full-time roles

willingness_to_pay.note: Multiple funded startups sell into this exact workflow

reachability.note: Distributors are listable, but the buyer is an operations director behind a gatekeeper

automation.note: Extraction is easy; writing into their ERP is the whole job

speed_to_revenue.note: Item-master matching must be built per customer before any value lands

whitespace.note: Several venture-funded companies own this wedge

opportunities.notes: Demand is beyond doubt. ERP write-access is the moat, and it is a moat against us, not for us.

opportunities.name: Bookkeeping cleanup & month-end close prep

willingness_to_pay.note: Offshore bookkeeping outsourcing is well established

whitespace.note: Mature offshore outsourcing market at low prices

opportunities.notes: Competing against established offshore labor at rates we cannot beat with a US-priced service.

opportunities.name: Insurance agency renewal processing & COI issuance

pain.note: Renewal season is a known crunch

reachability.note: State insurance departments publish licensed agency lists

automation.note: Agency management system access likely required

low_regulatory_risk.note: Issuing certificates may require a licensed producer

opportunities.notes: Licensing question needs answering before this could be pursued.

opportunities.name: RFP response library & drafting for staffing/IT firms
opportunities.buyer: Staffing, MSP, and IT services firms bidding regularly
opportunities.notes: Great deal size. Unpredictable workload spikes are a poor match for a fixed 6-10 hour week.

opportunities.name: Delivery-platform reconciliation & chargeback recovery
opportunities.buyer: Multi-location restaurants on third-party delivery platforms
kill_flags: Requires merchant-portal credentials for platforms whose terms of service restrict third-party access
opportunities.notes: Killed on the terms-of-service constraint. We do not build a business on access we are not permitted to have.
